findings.description: input.max_results is not validated. A negative value (e.g., -5) causes Array.prototype.slice(0, -5) to return all-but-last-5 entries (wrong subset) and sets truncated = (all.length > -5) which is always true. A NaN value causes slice(0, NaN) to return an empty array while truncated=true. A non-integer (e.g., 0.5) yields inconsistent truncation semantics. The tool should clamp/validate max_results to a non-negative integer before use.
findings.location: tools/search-files.ts: searchFiles, `const max = input.max_results ?? 100;` and subsequent slice/truncated computation

findings.description: Resource/DoS: vfs.search(input.root, input.needle) materializes the full result set into memory before max_results is applied via slice(). A broad needle (e.g., empty string or a very common substring) against a large VFS could produce an unbounded intermediate array, causing memory exhaustion regardless of max_results. The cap should be pushed down into the search call (pass max_results to vfs.search) or the search should be lazily/streamingly bounded.

input.root is forwarded to vfs.search without any validation/sanitization at this layer. If the VFS implementation performs prefix/string-based scoping or is backed by a real path, an attacker-controlled root (e.g., '/', '..', or an empty string) could widen the search scope beyond the intended subtree. Cannot be fully confirmed without the VFS implementation, but the tool performs no defensive check.

If vfs.search interprets `needle` as a regular expression (rather than a literal substring), an attacker-crafted needle could trigger ReDoS or regex-injection against VFS contents. The tool does not constrain or anchor the needle. Confirm VFS semantics; if regex is supported, a timeout or literal-only mode should be enforced.

summary: The tool is a thin wrapper and has no injection/SSRF/credential-leakage issues of its own, but it (1) fails to validate max_results, producing incorrect results/truncation flags for negative/NaN/non-integer inputs, and (2) loads the entire unbounded search result set into memory before applying the cap, a potential DoS vector. Lower-confidence notes flag missing root validation and possible ReDoS depending on VFS semantics. No error-handling gaps that leak sensitive info were found; exceptions from vfs.search propagate naturally.
